page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n2 family. It features 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The underlying hardware is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data places the n2-standard-8 in the average performance tier for most multi-core and memory operations. It achieves average results in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, passmark CPU score, and passmark memory score. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 413.79 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and approximately 50.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as AES encryption and single-threaded gzip compression, perform at average levels, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and physics simulations are weaker.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-standard-8 offers a standard resource density suitable for mainstream enterprise workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Given its balanced resource profile and average database operation benchmarks, it is appropriate for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate database operations. It is less suitable for compute-intensive physics simulations, heavy ray tracing, or large-scale LLM inference due to its weaker single-core and multi-threaded scaling in those specific areas.
